conventions.convention: Module categories have right C-actions. Left A-modules carry that action by P ⊙ X = P ⊗ X.

The right-action internal Hom represents Hom_C(X,[m,n]) = Hom_M(m ⊙ X,n). Its internal-end multiplication restricts to reversed ordinary composition. Functors from left A-modules to left B-modules correspond to B-A bimodules.
Tensor-algebra multiplication uses the positive middle crossing c_{B,A}; converting a right module action into a left action uses c_{Y,X}^{-1}.
The designated opposite algebra has multiplication m_A c_{A,A}^{-1}. The positive opposite has multiplication m_A c_{A,A}; the two are not identified.

In the algebra bicategory an A-B bimodule is an arrow A → B. Its action on left modules runs from B-modules to A-modules, so Mod(C) uses the 1-morphism opposite; this exchanges the left and right object-dual roles.

A fusion 2-category requires finite semisimplicity, a weak monoidal structure, a simple unit, and separate left and right object duals. No pivotal, spherical, dagger, or unitary enhancement is included.
The scalar pentagonator is ω on four homogeneous grades. Cochains are normalized at identity inputs, coefficients have trivial G-action, and the specified gauge direction is ω′ = ω δβ.

The general Mod(C) theorem assumes an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and full AC. Fusion-ring positive dimensions used for rank bounds are distinct from categorical squared norms; no pivotal structure is assumed.

load_bearing.statement: For a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the canonical Frobenius scalar t = λμΔη is nonzero and t^{-1}Δ is a K-bimodule section of multiplication.

For a fusion category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, Dim(C) = Σ_i |i|² is nonzero and λμΔη = Dim(C). Over C every |i|² is strictly positive real. No pivotal or unitary structure is assumed.

Every finite semisimple right C-module category over an algebraically closed field is equivalent to left modules over an internal-end algebra, without yet asserting separability. Right exact module functors from left A-modules to left B-modules correspond to B-A bimodules Q acting by Q ⊗_A −, including the equivalence on transformations.

For finite semisimple right module categories over a fusion category over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, Fun_C(M,N) is finite semisimple. Evaluation at the unit identifies Fun_C(C,C) with C and sends the identity functor to the tensor unit.

The specified normalized deformation complexes of module actions and module functors over a fusion category over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field admit a homotopy dh + hd = id in every positive degree.

For fixed characteristic-zero fusion data, indecomposable finite semisimple right module categories have rank at most floor(D), where D = Σ_i d_i² for the specified positive fusion-ring dimensions. Every action multiplicity satisfies n_{ai}^b ≤ D/d_i.

Assuming AC, fixed-rank finite semisimple right module structures over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero fusion category are represented by finitely many finite-type affine varieties; vanishing normalized degree-two deformation cohomology gives finitely many open change-of-basis orbits. Consequently there are finitely many indecomposable module categories up to module equivalence.

For right module categories represented by separable algebras A and B in a braided fusion category, the stated relative Deligne product is represented by left modules over the positive braided tensor algebra A ⊗ B. These products assemble into a weak monoidal 2-category.

In the stated separable-algebra/bimodule monoidal 2-category, a separable algebra A has a left dual represented by the negative opposite and a right dual represented by the positive opposite, with invertible cusp maps for both snake composites.
For a finite group G and normalized group 4-cocycle ω:G⁴ → C×, the specified convolution and scalar pentagonator make 2Vect_G^ω a fusion 2-category, with simple-object classes exactly δ_g.

If ω′ = ω δβ for a normalized 3-cochain β, the identity graded 2-functor with the specified scalar triple coherence is a monoidal 2-equivalence. Within this identity-on-grading gauge family, untwisting exists exactly when [ω] = 0.
